searchText: I apologize for starting a morbid discussion, but what would it happen to Ethereum in a nuclear war?For the sake of the argument, let's say a war that takes down permanently 60-70% of nodes in US and Europe. Do we think the p2p layer could still work? How about the consensus layer? I think if nuclear war ever happens and 60-70% of EU/US population wipes out, there are more important problems to deal with 😅 If the banking/credit sector is down, having some form of digital money that works would be good. Beside a lot of people reside outside of US/EU.. Ethereum will continue working, just without finalization and overall stability Also radiation has no borders, it will spread worldwide Cough cough, physical money is what people will use when the internet is down everywhere. Bottle caps or more realistically food and water. The Chinese used tea bricks and that system with rations or water could be used. i don't want to enter a discussion if my question make sense or not. I want just an honest answer 😄 I’d assume the network chugs along just validators will miss blocks and be slashed until all the downed validators are gone for example, what is the impact of a lot of nodes dropping out on the p2p network? or.. to how many node the average node is connected? would be interesting to study also what type of network partitions would happen.. in general.. a global network partition can be caused by other things than a nuclear war https://ethernodes.org/ is this accurate? that's our best guess at the number of nodes globaly? is there something similar for the beacon chain? it will depend if the nuke headed to Virginia are intercepted or not because most of nodes are in aws virginia? Lol, good one how is even possible for Brazil to have just 7 nodes.. with 200m people living there it's sad though hardware costs twice as much in brazil as they have a 100% import tax on tech, it is worse than austrailia anyone have a copy of the entire chain being saved somewhere that will survive at least a few nukes in different locations, and a tsunami from the coast, and an EMP? Aws brazil is much more expensive even if you live there you’ll host the nodes somewhere cheaper
